title: Pharmacy / chronic-script exit
summary: Leaving Singapore on chronic meds — pull last refills, request transfer letters, and float private-script cash before clinic accounts and Singpass logistics change.

sections.title: Inventory every chronic script still active
sections.body: GP, polyclinic, and specialist scripts often renew on different calendars. Before you freeze clinic portals or change Singpass factors, list every ongoing medicine, dose, and next refill date. Photograph bottle labels and the latest prescription printouts — overseas pharmacies rarely accept a WhatsApp photo as a valid transfer.
bullets: List active chronic meds with dose, frequency, and next refill window
Photograph labels and keep PDF/print copies of current prescriptions
Note which scripts sit at polyclinic vs private GP vs specialist

sections.title: Book last refills before fly week
sections.body: Many leavers discover mid-packing that a 30-day supply ends three days after landing. Ask clinics whether a travel / longer fill is allowed, and keep a SGD float for private top-ups when polyclinic slots are full. Sketch cash on /tools/pharmacy-last-refill-float so packing week does not raid the clinic-deposit pot.
bullets: Ask for travel or extended fills in writing where the clinic allows it
Hold a separate last-refill float from clinic deposit cash

sections.title: Request transfer / summary letters for the next GP
sections.body: A destination GP usually wants a diagnosis list, current doses, and recent labs — not a bag of half-used blister packs alone. Request medical summaries and script histories while you still have Singapore contact numbers and can collect sealed letters. Do not assume clinic portals stay reachable after pass cancellation.
bullets: Request a medical summary and active-medication list before the last consult
Collect sealed letters or portal PDFs while login still works
Pair clinic account close with /tools/clinic-deposit-exit if deposits remain

sections.title: Controlled meds and carry-on documentation
sections.body: Some chronic meds need original packaging, scripts, and destination import rules. Confirm what you can legally carry in hand luggage, and keep doctor letters with the medicines — not in checked bags. Folklore from expat chats is not customs advice.
bullets: Check destination import rules for each controlled or injectable medicine
Pack scripts and doctor letters with the meds in carry-on
Do not treat forum packing lists as legal clearance

sections.title: Clinic portals, Singpass, and contact hygiene
sections.body: Prescription renewals and appointment SMS often depend on a Singapore number and Singpass. Update email contacts, download histories, and sequence Singpass factor changes after pharmacy and clinic exports are done — the same week CPF and bank archives often collide.
bullets: Download clinic portal histories before SIM / Singpass factor changes
Keep one inbox alive for pharmacy or clinic callbacks during notice week

sections.title: Same-week stack with hospital and leaving playbooks
sections.body: Chronic refills, hospital deposit returns, and leaving checklists often share one fortnight. Sequence last pharmacy visits while clinic accounts are still open, then deposit clearances, then physical leaving tasks — so meds and letters are not trapped behind a closed portal.
bullets: Put last refill, transfer letters, and clinic deposit return on one calendar
Pair with /journeys/hospital-cash-deposit when inpatient deposits remain
Keep one adult free for pharmacy or clinic callbacks during packing week
